claims.text: Role in takotsubo: ACEis or ARBs may help LV recovery;
claims.quote: Angiotensin-converting-enzyme inhibitors (ACEi) or angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARB) may potentially facilitate LV recovery.
The use of ACEi or ARB was associated with improved survival at 1-year follow-up even after propensity matching.
whereas ACEi or ARB are associated with a lower prevalence of recurrence. The significance of this observation remains uncertain and requires validation in other cohorts.

claims.text: Valsartan: K-sparing diuretics, K supplements, K-containing salt substitutes or heparin can raise K (and creatinine in HF);
claims.quote: Concomitant use of valsartan with other agents that block the renin-angiotensin system, potassium-sparing diuretics (e.g., spironolactone, triamterene, amiloride), potassium supplements, salt substitutes containing potassium or other drugs that may increase potassium levels (e.g., heparin) may lead to increases in serum potassium and in heart failure patients to increases in serum creatinine.

claims.text: dual RAS blockade (ARB + ACE-I or aliskiren) raises hypotension, hyperkalemia and renal-failure risk.
claims.quote: Dual blockade of the RAS with angiotensin receptor blockers, ACE inhibitors, or aliskiren is associated with increased risks of hypotension, hyperkalemia, and changes in renal function (including acute renal failure) compared to monotherapy.
claims.locator: 7.3 Dual Blockade of the Renin-Angiotensin System (RAS)

claims.text: Valsartan: advise pts ⍉ to use salt substitutes w.o asking their provider (hyperkalemia).
claims.quote: Hyperkalemia: Advise patients not to use salt substitutes without consulting their healthcare provider [see Drug Interactions (7.1)] .
